Definition: of Hebrew origin (H6635 in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God:--sabaoth.
BiblicalUsage: The Greek word sabaṓth means armies; sabaoth (that is tsebaoth), a military epithet of God. It stands in Romans 9:29, "…Esaias said before, Except the Lord of Sabaoth…", and in James 5:4, "…labourers who have reaped down your fields, which…" — in the SBL text the word stands as Σαβαώθ.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe God put sabaṓth here on purpose, and I take his word for it.
